prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1279; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection and said the other vehicle crossed into their lane. The claimant was identified as the driver of the vehicle, and the police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 2: The driver is named on the policy, and the policy was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.

Entry 3: Photos taken at the scene confirm some of the reported details, including the location of the impact and the rough resting positions of both vehicles. No independent witnesses have come forward to describe how the collision occurred.

Entry 4: The claimant was contacted by phone and described the collision and the onset of back pain in the same way as in the first conversation. The account has remained consistent across every contact so far.

Entry 5: The claimant reports a back strain and has been seen at a clinic for treatment. The treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of injury, so the file will be monitored.

Entry 6: No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the claimant's history or from prior claims. It is not yet clear whether the back injury was caused by this collision or by something else.

Entry 7: The vehicle was inspected at a repair facility. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from our records or from the inspection.

Entry 8: The inspection found damage to the front bumper, hood, and radiator support. It is not yet clear whether all of the damage came from this impact, so the repair estimate is being reviewed line by line.

Entry 9: The repair estimate has been sent to the body shop for a second look at the areas that may have been damaged in an earlier event. The shop has been asked to note which parts were visibly damaged in the photos.

Entry 10: The claim file has been reviewed against the photos, the police report, and the statements taken so far. The core facts of the collision are supported, but the extent of the injury and vehicle damage still needs work.

Entry 11: A request for the claimant's medical records has been sent with their consent. Once the records arrive, the causation question on the back injury will be revisited with the treating provider.

Entry 12: The file remains open pending receipt of the medical records and the final repair figures. The next review is scheduled once those items are in.
